CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old male with longstanding hypertension since young age presents for evaluation. Patient reports recent emergency room visit in March with elevated blood pressure and palpitations. Patient attributes this episode to consumption of several cups of coffee without breakfast and believes it was likely a panic attack rather than true cardiac pathology. Denies recurrence of palpitations since that time. Patient reports blood pressure has been running 146-155 mmHg in the mornings on home monitoring. Recently started on new antihypertensive regimen by new primary care doctor approximately one month ago. Patient is attempting to reduce salt intake and exercises on treadmill when able.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, dizziness, or other acute complaints. No abdominal pain on examination.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension (longstanding, since young age)
Recent palpitations with emergency room evaluation in March 2026

MEDICATIONS
Benicar HCT (Olmesartan-Hydrochlorothiazide 40-25 mg) - started approximately one month ago
Amlodipine 10 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Multiple family members with hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with girlfriend. Exercises on treadmill when able. Attempting to reduce dietary salt intake. Does not consume excessive caffeine regularly.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well.
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs appreciated.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender throughout.
Extremities: No edema noted in ankles or feet bilaterally.

RESULTS
Potassium level one week ago: 4.0 mEq/L (normal)
Thyroid profile from March 1, 2021 - copied forward per documentation request

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Resistant hypertension on three maximally dosed medications with blood pressure still not at goal. Patient discussed possibility of secondary causes of hypertension including hyperaldosteronism. Adding spironolactone to current antihypertensive regimen. Patient counseled on potential side effects including dizziness, electrolyte disturbances (hyperkalemia and hyponatremia), and rare risk of gynecomastia (1 in 100 males). Patient educated on importance of hydration and need for repeat blood work in two weeks to monitor potassium and sodium levels. Patient counseled on lifestyle modifications including DASH diet, salt restriction to less than 2000 mg daily (goal 1500 mg daily), and regular aerobic exercise for 30 minutes most days. Provided education regarding heart.org website and DASH diet resources. Follow-up appointment in two weeks for blood pressure check and metabolic panel. If uncontrolled on spironolactone, will refer to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of procedure-based therapies such as renal denervation.
